Test-set comparison

The notebook doesn't ship with pre-executed outputs, so no numbers are fabricated here — run it end-to-end in Colab or locally to populate this table on your own machine. All five models are scored identically on NASA's official, held-out FD001 test engines.

Model Test MAE (cycles) Test RMSE Test R²

MAE

Mean Absolute Error — average absolute difference between predicted and true RUL, in cycles. The most directly interpretable metric here.

RMSE

Root Mean Squared Error — like MAE but penalizes large errors more heavily.

R²

Coefficient of determination — how much of the variance in true RUL is explained by the model's predictions.

Two questions worth checking once you have results: does any PyTorch model actually beat the Random Forest benchmark? And do the recurrent models (LSTM/GRU) outperform the simpler MLP/CNN — i.e. does explicit sequence order help on this particular fault mode?

Limitations & possible extensions

  • Single sub-dataset: only FD001 (1 operating condition, 1 fault mode) is used. FD002–FD004 add multiple operating conditions and a second fault mode, which typically requires per-condition normalization instead of a single global standardization.
  • Fixed training budget: 10 epochs, no learning-rate scheduling, no early stopping, and no hyperparameter search — the comparison is meant to be a fair like-for-like baseline across architectures, not a tuned leaderboard entry.
  • Single train/validation split: one GroupShuffleSplit, not k-fold cross-validation, so validation metrics carry some split-to-split variance.
  • No attention-based or Transformer sequence model is included alongside the MLP/CNN/LSTM/GRU comparison.
  • No official PHM scoring function: the standard C-MAPSS literature also reports an asymmetric "PHM score" that penalizes late predictions more than early ones; this project reports MAE/RMSE/R² only.

Reproduce this table

git clone https://github.com/shravanvinayhegde/Predictive-Maintenance-PyTorch.git
cd Predictive-Maintenance-PyTorch
jupyter notebook NASA_pytorch.ipynb

Or open it directly in Colab — no manual dataset download required, the first two cells fetch and extract C-MAPSS FD001 automatically. A CUDA GPU is optional; device selection is automatic.
